listen.script: Hi everyone, this is Noura. I just wanted to tell you about the science fair. Originally it was going to be held in the main hall on Thursday, but because the hall is being repainted, it's been moved to the library. The date hasn't changed, though. Oh, and one more thing. Instead of bringing your projects in the morning, please drop them off the afternoon before, so the teachers have time to set everything up.
listen.q: What has changed about the science fair?
options: The day it takes place and the place where it is held
The place where it is held and when students bring their projects
The time it starts and the teachers who organise it

listen.script: Boy: So, did you enjoy the new adventure film at the weekend? Everyone's been talking about it. Girl: Well, the special effects were amazing, I'll give it that. But honestly, I'd guessed the ending within about twenty minutes, and some of the characters were so annoying. I'm glad I saw it on the big screen, but I wouldn't bother watching it again.
listen.q: What is the girl's overall opinion of the film?
options: She was impressed by how it looked but disappointed by the story.
She found it so exciting that she wants to see it again.
She thought it was too long and the effects were poor.

read.passage: When fifteen-year-old Reem from Jeddah noticed how much plastic was left on the beach after weekend picnics, she decided she couldn't just ignore it. At first, she simply collected rubbish with her younger brother every Friday morning. However, after posting a few photos online, she was surprised to find that dozens of students from other schools wanted to join in. Within six months, her small idea had grown into a volunteer group of over eighty teenagers. Reem admits that organising so many people has not always been easy. 'There were weeks when only three people turned up, and I seriously considered giving up,' she says. What kept her going was seeing families start to bring their own bags to take rubbish home. Local businesses have since donated gloves and bins, and the city council has asked her group to help design a campaign for primary schools.

qs.q: Why did Reem's project grow so quickly?
options: The city council asked her to organise a large group.
Other young people saw what she was doing online and wanted to help.
Local businesses paid students to take part.

qs.q: What motivated Reem to continue during difficult times?
options: Noticing a positive change in people's behaviour
Being able to spend time with her brother

speak.prompt: Some people think that teenagers should spend part of their summer holidays doing volunteer work in their community. What is your opinion? Give reasons and examples, and say whether there could be any disadvantages.
speak.expect: A B2 learner can give a clear, developed point of view and support it with relevant reasons and examples (e.g. helping at a charity, a mosque or a hospital, gaining experience). They can explain advantages and disadvantages of the idea and consider another perspective (e.g. 'On the other hand, students also need time to rest'). They speak with reasonable fluency and spontaneity for 1-2 minutes with few long pauses, link ideas using a range of connectors (however, as a result, whereas, apart from that), and use a range of structures (conditionals, modals such as 'should' and 'might', some complex sentences) with good control. Occasional errors do not cause misunderstanding, and they can often self-correct. Vocabulary is sufficient for the topic, using some less common words (e.g. 'responsibility', 'benefit', 'experience'), with some circumlocution where needed. Pronunciation is clear and intelligible, with generally appropriate word and sentence stress.
